units.context: Section 22 of the CGST Act, 2017 (liability to GST registration), 22 Explanation: this unit forms part of the provision governing liability to GST registration.

summary_check.issues: Omits that subsection (2) expressly overrides section 22(1) and section 24, subject to notified conditions and restrictions.
summary_check.corrected_summary: Persons exclusively supplying non-taxable or wholly exempt goods or services, and agriculturists to the extent of produce from cultivation of land, are not liable to registration. On the Council's recommendation, the Government may notify additional exempt categories subject to conditions and restrictions notwithstanding section 22(1) or section 24.

metadata_check.issues: Omits the express overriding effect of subsection (2) over section 22(1) and compulsory registration under section 24.

links.evidence: Section 23(2) applies notwithstanding anything contrary in section 22(1).
Section 23(2) expressly overrides section 24 for notified registration-exempt categories.
Section 23(1)(b) uses agriculturist as defined in section 2(7), with relief limited to produce from cultivation of land.

answers_questions: Who is not liable to GST registration?
What is the scope of registration relief for an agriculturist?
Can a notified registration exemption override compulsory registration?

summary_check.issues: Irrespective of other provisions overstates the clause, which names section 22(1); section 23(2) expressly overrides section 24. Also omits overseas online money gaming suppliers.
summary_check.corrected_summary: Section 24 requires specified categories to register notwithstanding section 22(1), including inter-State taxable suppliers, casual and non-resident taxable persons, reverse-charge payers, section 9(5) liable persons, TDS deductors, taxable-person agents, ISDs and specified e-commerce suppliers and operators. It also covers overseas OIDAR suppliers to persons in India other than registered persons, overseas online money gaming suppliers to persons in India, and notified classes; section 23(2) permits notified registration exemptions overriding this section.

metadata_check.issues: Applies_to omits overseas online money gaming suppliers in clause (xia); e-commerce suppliers exclude section 9(5) supplies under clause (ix). Section 24 does not override all provisions: section 23(2) expressly permits notified exemptions.

links.evidence: Opening words impose specified compulsory registration notwithstanding section 22(1).
Section 23(2) permits notified registration exemptions notwithstanding section 24.
Section 24(iv) covers persons liable under section 9(5), and clause (ix) excludes supplies specified under that subsection.
Section 24(vi) covers section 51 tax deductors whether or not separately registered.
Section 24(ix)-(x) refers to electronic commerce operators required to collect tax at source under section 52.
Persons liable under section 24 follow the registration procedure in section 25.

answers_questions: Who must register irrespective of the section 22(1) turnover threshold?
Which electronic commerce suppliers and operators fall within section 24?
When must overseas OIDAR and online money gaming suppliers register?
Can a notified section 23(2) exemption override section 24?
